name: Adam
summary: The first human, formed from the dust of the ground and placed in the Garden of Eden to tend it. His disobedience with Eve, eating the forbidden fruit, brought sin and death into the world.

name: Eve
summary: The first woman, formed from Adam's rib and called 'the mother of all living.' Deceived by the serpent, she ate the forbidden fruit and shared it with Adam.

name: Cain
summary: Adam and Eve's firstborn, a farmer. When his offering was not accepted and his brother's was, he killed Abel in the field, and was sent out as a wanderer under God's protective mark.

name: Abel
summary: Adam and Eve's second son, a shepherd. He brought the firstborn of his flock and God accepted it — and his brother killed him for it.

name: Noah
summary: A righteous man in a corrupt generation, instructed by God to build an ark to save his family and pairs of every animal from a great flood.

name: Abraham
summary: Called by God to leave his homeland for a land he would be shown, and promised he would become the father of a great nation. Originally named Abram.

name: Sarah
summary: Abraham's wife, who remained childless into old age until God fulfilled his promise and she gave birth to Isaac. Originally named Sarai.

name: Hagar
summary: Sarah's Egyptian servant, given to Abraham to bear a child. Mistreated and twice driven into the wilderness, she is the only person in Genesis to give God a name: the God who sees me.

name: Lot
summary: Abraham's nephew, who left Haran with him. Given first choice of the land he took the well-watered Jordan valley, settled toward Sodom, and had to be pulled out of it by angels.

name: Ishmael
summary: Abraham's firstborn, born to Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian servant. Sent away with his mother after Isaac was born, but God promised to make him into a great nation as well.

name: Isaac
summary: The long-promised son of Abraham and Sarah. As a young man he was offered by Abraham as a sacrifice in a test of faith, then spared by God's provision of a ram.

name: Rebekah
summary: Isaac's wife, chosen at a well by Abraham's servant. Mother of twins Jacob and Esau, she favored Jacob and helped him secure his father's blessing.

name: Esau
summary: Isaac and Rebekah's elder twin, a skilled hunter who sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew and was later denied their father's primary blessing.

name: Jacob
summary: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, who obtained his brother Esau's birthright and blessing. Later renamed Israel after wrestling with God, he fathered twelve sons who became the twelve tribes of Israel.

name: Rachel
summary: The younger daughter of Laban, whom Jacob loved and worked fourteen years for. Barren for years while her sister bore sons, she became the mother of Joseph and died bearing Benjamin.

name: Leah
summary: Laban's elder daughter, given to Jacob in place of Rachel. Unloved but not unseen — God opened her womb, and her fourth son Judah became the line of the kings.

name: Joseph
summary: Jacob's favored son, sold into slavery in Egypt by his jealous brothers. Rose to become second-in-command to Pharaoh, and later saved his family from famine.

name: Moses
summary: Born under a death sentence and hidden in a basket on the Nile, raised in Pharaoh's own household, and forty years later called by name out of a bush that would not burn out. He would lead Israel out of Egypt.

name: Jochebed
roles: hid her son in defiance of Pharaoh
mother of Moses, Aaron and Miriam
summary: A Hebrew woman who hid her infant son three months, then risked the river rather than Pharaoh's decree — and was hired, without Pharaoh's daughter ever knowing who she was, to nurse her own child.

name: Miriam
summary: Moses' older sister, who watched from a distance as the basket drifted, then stepped forward with exactly the right question to put her own mother at her brother's side.

name: Aaron
summary: Moses' elder brother, sent by God into the wilderness to meet him and become the voice of a man who called himself slow of speech.

name: Pharaoh's Daughter
summary: An Egyptian princess who found a Hebrew baby in the reeds, had compassion on him despite knowing exactly who he was, and raised her own people's intended victim in the palace itself.

name: Zipporah
roles: met at a well in Midian
summary: A priest of Midian's daughter, one of seven sisters Moses defended at a well. She became his wife during his forty years in exile, and bore him a son.

name: Naomi
roles: lost everything, then found fullness again
summary: Widowed and left childless in Moab, she returned to Bethlehem calling herself Mara — bitter — and left it again a grandmother, in the family line of David.

name: Ruth
roles: stayed when she could have gone home
summary: A Moabite widow who refused to leave her mother-in-law, gleaned in a stranger's field to keep them both alive, and asked for redemption rather than charity. Her line runs to David, and further.

name: Boaz
summary: A prosperous relative of Naomi's dead husband, who noticed a foreign gleaner in his field, protected her, and redeemed her family's inheritance and her future when a nearer relative would not.

name: Elimelech
summary: Naomi's husband, who took his family from Bethlehem to Moab to escape a famine, and died there before ever seeing them return.

name: Orpah
summary: Naomi's other daughter-in-law, who loved her enough to weep at their parting, but chose — reasonably, and without condemnation in the text — to return to her own people and gods rather than follow her into an uncertain future.

name: Pharaoh
roles: let Egypt's firstborn die rather than let Israel go
summary: The king of Egypt who enslaved Israel and refused, plague after plague, to let them go. The text never gives him a name — he represents the throne more than a single ruler across the narrative.

name: Joshua
roles: wouldn't leave the Tent of Meeting
summary: Moses' young aide, first seen leading Israel's fighting men against Amalek and lingering in the tent of meeting after Moses left it. He becomes the far more central figure who leads Israel into the promised land.

name: Nadab
summary: Aaron's oldest son, ordained a priest alongside his father and brothers — and killed by fire from Yahweh days later for offering incense God never commanded.

name: Abihu
summary: Aaron's second son, ordained alongside his brother Nadab and killed with him the same way, in the same moment.

name: Caleb
roles: believed they could take the land
summary: One of the twelve spies sent into Canaan, and one of only two who came back saying Israel could take it. For that, he was the only man of his generation, besides Joshua, who lived to enter the land.

name: Korah
summary: A Levite who led an open challenge to Moses and Aaron's authority, claiming the whole congregation was equally holy. The ground opened beneath him, his fellow rebels, and their households.

name: Eleazar
summary: Aaron's son, given his father's priestly garments on Mount Hor the day Aaron died. He carries the priesthood forward into the next generation.

name: Balaam
summary: A foreign prophet hired by a Moabite king to curse Israel. His own donkey saw the angel blocking the road before he did — and when he finally spoke over Israel, blessing came out instead of the curse he was paid for.

name: Rahab
roles: chose Israel's God over her own people
summary: A woman of Jericho who hid two Israelite spies on her roof, believing Yahweh had already given them the land. She and her family were the only ones spared when the city fell.

name: Achan
summary: A man of Judah who secretly took silver, gold, and a robe from Jericho's forbidden plunder. Israel was routed at Ai until he was found out and stoned.

name: Ehud
summary: A left-handed Benjamite who hid a sword on his right thigh where no one would think to check, got Moab's king alone in a private room, and delivered Israel from Moabite oppression with it.

name: Deborah
roles: prophetess who led an army into battle
summary: A prophetess who judged Israel and summoned Barak to fight the army oppressing them. When he refused to go without her, she agreed — and told him the real victory would belong to a woman instead.

name: Barak
summary: Summoned by Deborah to fight Sisera's army, he agreed only on the condition that she come with him — and so the honor of the victory went to a woman instead of him.

name: Sisera
roles: killed by a woman with a tent peg
summary: The commander of the army oppressing Israel for twenty years. Routed in battle, he fled on foot to what he thought was a safe tent — and was killed there in his sleep.

name: Jael
roles: killed Sisera in her own tent
summary: A Kenite woman who welcomed the fleeing general Sisera into her tent, gave him milk and a place to sleep, and killed him there with a tent peg and a hammer.

name: Gideon
roles: threshed wheat in hiding out of fear
summary: Found threshing wheat in a wine press to hide it from raiders, he was called a mighty man of valor by an angel while insisting he was the least in the weakest family in his tribe. He tested God twice with a fleece before believing — then watched his army shrink to three hundred men so no one could claim Israel saved itself.

name: Jephthah
roles: an outcast who became a deliverer
kept a vow that cost him his daughter
summary: Driven out by his half-brothers, he became a skilled fighter and was called back to lead Israel against Ammon. He vowed to sacrifice whatever came out of his house first if he won — and his only child came out to celebrate with him.

name: Jephthah's Daughter
roles: mourned two months in the mountains
summary: Jephthah's only child, who ran out to celebrate her father's victory with tambourines and dancing — not knowing what he had vowed. She asked only for two months to mourn with her friends before he kept his word.

name: Samson
roles: brought down a temple in his death
summary: Born to a once-childless woman and set apart to God from the womb, his uncut hair carried strength no army could match. Betrayed by the one weakness he never guarded, he died pulling down a temple on the people who blinded him.

name: Delilah
roles: discovered the secret of Samson's strength
summary: A woman Samson loved, paid by Philistine rulers to find out what made him strong. She wore him down with the same question until he finally told her the truth.

name: Hannah
summary: Barren and taunted for it, she vowed that if God gave her a son she would give him back to serve at the tabernacle for life — then kept her vow and sang instead of grieving.

name: Eli
summary: The priest who raised Samuel at the tabernacle and taught him to recognize God's voice. He died the moment he heard the ark had been captured, at the end of a long life spent failing to restrain his own corrupt sons.

name: Samuel
roles: heard God's voice as a boy
summary: Given to the tabernacle before he could remember anything else, he became the last judge and the prophet who anointed both Saul and David — the hinge between the age of judges and the age of kings.

name: Saul
summary: Chosen as Israel's first king from the smallest family in the smallest tribe, he disobeyed two direct commands, was told his kingdom would not endure, and spent his final years hunting the man God had already chosen to replace him.

name: David
roles: the shepherd chosen when no one else was
summary: The youngest of eight brothers, out with the sheep when Samuel came looking for a king, chosen because Yahweh looks at the heart rather than appearance. He kills Goliath with a sling, befriends Jonathan, and refuses twice to kill the king who is hunting him.

name: Goliath
summary: A nine-foot Philistine champion who taunted Israel's army for forty days before a shepherd boy with no armor and a sling ended it.

name: Jonathan
roles: loved David as his own soul
summary: Saul's son and heir to the throne, who loved David more than his own claim to it, made a covenant with him, warned him of his father's murderous intent, and died alongside Saul on Mount Gilboa.

name: Michal
roles: Saul's daughter who despised David's worship
summary: David's first wife and Saul's daughter; watching him dance before the ark, she despises him for it and remains childless the rest of her life.

name: Bathsheba
roles: the wife David took by force, mother of Solomon
summary: Uriah's wife, taken by David while her husband was at war; later becomes the mother of Solomon.

name: Uriah
roles: the loyal soldier David had killed to cover his sin
summary: A Hittite soldier in David's army, more loyal to his fellow soldiers than to his own comfort; killed on David's orders to hide David's adultery with his wife.

name: Nathan
roles: the prophet who told David "you are the man"
summary: A prophet in David's court who delivers God's covenant promise, then later confronts David's sin with a parable that leaves the king condemning himself.

name: Absalom
roles: David's son who avenged his sister and later rebelled against him
summary: David's third son; kills his half-brother Amnon for raping their sister Tamar, then years later steals the loyalty of Israel and drives David out of Jerusalem.

name: Tamar
roles: David's daughter, raped by her half-brother Amnon
summary: David's daughter and Absalom's full sister; raped by their half-brother Amnon, an act her brother avenges two years later.

name: Amnon
roles: David's firstborn son, who forced his half-sister Tamar
summary: David's oldest son; obsessed with his half-sister Tamar, rapes her and then discards her, and is later killed for it by her brother Absalom.

name: Mephibosheth
roles: Jonathan's crippled son, shown kindness for his father's sake
summary: Jonathan's son, crippled in both feet since childhood; David seeks him out and restores Saul's land to him for Jonathan's sake.

name: Joab
roles: David's ruthless army commander, loyal but uncontrollable
summary: The commander of David's army; carries out the order that gets Uriah killed, and later kills Absalom against David's direct command.

name: Solomon
roles: asked for wisdom instead of riches, built the temple
summary: David and Bathsheba's son; asks God for an understanding heart rather than wealth, builds the temple in Jerusalem, but his foreign wives turn his heart to other gods in his old age.

name: Adonijah
roles: David's son who crowned himself king too soon
summary: David's older son, who declares himself king while his father is still alive and dying, before Solomon is chosen instead.

name: The queen of Sheba
roles: tested Solomon's wisdom and found it exceeded the reports
summary: A foreign queen who travels to Jerusalem to test Solomon's famous wisdom with hard questions, and leaves saying not even half of it had been told her.

name: Rehoboam
roles: Solomon's son whose harsh answer split the kingdom
summary: Solomon's son and successor; rejects the elders' counsel to ease the people's burden, and loses ten of Israel's twelve tribes to Jeroboam on the spot.

name: Jeroboam
roles: led ten tribes away and built golden calves to keep them from Jerusalem
summary: An official under Solomon who becomes king over the ten northern tribes when they reject Rehoboam, then sets up rival golden-calf worship so his people won't return to Jerusalem.

name: Elijah
roles: the prophet who called down fire on Mount Carmel
summary: A prophet from Gilead who confronts king Ahab over Baal worship, is fed by ravens and a foreign widow through a famine, wins a public contest against 450 prophets of Baal, and meets God in a still small voice at Horeb.

name: The widow of Zarephath
roles: the foreign widow whose flour and oil never ran out
summary: A widow in Sidon down to her last handful of flour, who feeds Elijah first at his word and finds her jar never runs empty through the whole famine.

name: Ahab
roles: the king who married Jezebel and stole Naboth's vineyard
summary: King of Israel, married to Jezebel; promotes Baal worship, loses the Carmel contest to Elijah, and lets his wife arrange a man's murder so he can take his vineyard.

name: Jezebel
roles: Ahab's wife who had Naboth killed for his vineyard
summary: Ahab's wife, a promoter of Baal worship who arranges false charges to have Naboth stoned to death so Ahab can take his vineyard.

name: Naboth
roles: killed on false charges so Ahab could take his vineyard
summary: A landowner in Jezreel who refuses to sell his family's inherited vineyard to king Ahab, and is falsely accused and stoned to death for it.

name: Elisha
roles: Elijah's successor, the prophet of everyday miracles
summary: Elijah's attendant and chosen successor, who receives a double portion of his spirit and spends decades working quiet miracles for widows, foreigners, and armies across the northern kingdom.

name: Naaman
roles: the Aramean commander healed of leprosy in the Jordan
summary: A Syrian army commander with leprosy who almost refuses Elisha's unglamorous instructions, then is healed and declares there is no God anywhere but in Israel.

name: Gehazi
roles: Elisha's servant, struck with leprosy for his greed
summary: Elisha's attendant, who chases Naaman down for a gift his master had refused, and carries away Naaman's leprosy as the price.

name: The Shunammite woman
roles: the woman who housed Elisha and got her dead son back
summary: A well-off woman of Shunem who builds Elisha a room, is given the son she never expected, and rides straight to the prophet when the boy suddenly dies.

name: Jehu
roles: the army commander anointed to end the house of Ahab
summary: An army commander anointed king by a prophet to wipe out Ahab's dynasty and avenge Jezebel's murders of God's prophets.

name: Hezekiah
roles: Judah's king who trusted Yahweh against Assyria
summary: A king of Judah who trusted Yahweh more than any king before or after him; he laid the Assyrian threat before God in prayer and was delivered, and was later given fifteen added years of life.

name: Sennacherib
roles: the Assyrian king whose army was struck outside Jerusalem
summary: The king of Assyria who mocked Hezekiah's trust in God, then lost 185,000 men in a single night and withdrew.

name: Isaiah
roles: the prophet whose call vision and oracles of judgment and comfort span decades of Judah's kings
summary: A prophet in Judah across the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, called in a vision of Yahweh's holiness that left him undone until a coal from the altar purified his lips. He warned of coming judgment, assured Hezekiah that Jerusalem would stand against Assyria and that his life would be extended, and spoke some of the Old Testament's most enduring words of comfort and hope for a people not yet delivered.

name: Josiah
roles: the boy king who rediscovered the law and purged Judah's idols
summary: Made king of Judah at eight; when the lost Book of the Law was found and read to him, he tore his clothes, renewed the covenant, and tore down every idol and high place in the land.

name: Huldah
roles: the prophetess who authenticated the Book of the Law
summary: A prophetess in Jerusalem whom Josiah's officials consult about the rediscovered law; she confirms the coming judgment but says it will not fall in Josiah's lifetime.

name: Nebuchadnezzar
roles: the Babylonian king who burned Jerusalem, then was humbled into acknowledging Daniel's God
summary: The king of Babylon who besieged Jerusalem, destroyed the temple, and carried Judah into exile. In his own court he was outmatched by Daniel's wisdom, watched three Jewish exiles walk unharmed out of a furnace he built to kill them, and was struck with madness for seven years after boasting over his own greatness -- restored only once he acknowledged that the Most High rules every kingdom.

name: Zedekiah
roles: the last king of Judah, blinded and carried to Babylon
summary: The final king of Judah; his rebellion against Babylon brought the siege that ended the kingdom, and he was forced to watch his sons killed before being blinded and exiled.

name: Abijah
roles: the king of Judah who won a battle by relying on Yahweh
summary: Rehoboam's son and successor in Judah; outnumbered by Jeroboam's army, he called Israel to stop fighting against God, and Judah prevailed because they relied on Yahweh.

name: Asa
roles: the reforming king of Judah who later trusted Aram over God
summary: A king of Judah who tore down idols and cried to Yahweh against a vast army early in his reign, but late in life bought off Syria with temple silver and was rebuked for it.

name: Jehoshaphat
roles: the king of Judah who sent singers ahead of his army
summary: A king of Judah who had the law taught town to town, and who met an invasion by gathering the nation to pray and sending the temple choir out in front of the soldiers.

name: Joash
roles: the boy king who restored the temple, then killed the priest's son
summary: Hidden as an infant and crowned at seven by the priest Jehoiada; he restored the temple while Jehoiada lived, but after the priest died he turned to idols and had Jehoiada's son Zechariah stoned.

name: Jehoiada
roles: the priest who hid the heir of David's line and crowned him king
summary: The high priest who sheltered the infant Joash through Athaliah's purge, overthrew her, crowned the boy king, and guided Judah back to Yahweh for as long as he lived.

name: Zechariah son of Jehoiada
roles: the priest stoned in the temple court for rebuking Joash
summary: Jehoiada's son; when he rebuked king Joash for abandoning Yahweh, Joash had him stoned in the courtyard of the temple. His dying words were "May Yahweh see, and avenge."

name: Uzziah
roles: the king who prospered while he sought God, then was struck with leprosy for his pride
summary: A long-reigning, successful king of Judah whose heart was lifted up once he was strong; he forced his way into the temple to burn incense and was a leper from that day.

name: Manasseh
roles: Judah's most idolatrous king, who repented in a Babylonian prison
summary: The king who filled even the temple with altars to other gods; carried to Babylon in chains, he humbled himself and prayed, was restored to Jerusalem, and spent his last years tearing out the idols he had raised.

name: Cyrus
roles: the Persian king whose decree opened the road home from exile
summary: The king of Persia who, after seventy years of exile, proclaimed that Yahweh had charged him to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem and that any of God's people who wished could go up.

name: Zerubbabel
roles: the governor who led the first return and laid the temple's foundation
summary: Descendant of David and governor of Judah who led the first wave of exiles home from Babylon under Cyrus's decree. With the priest Jeshua he rebuilt the altar despite fear of the surrounding peoples, then saw the temple's foundation laid and, years later, the house itself finished.

name: Jeshua
roles: the high priest who rebuilt the altar with Zerubbabel
summary: The high priest who returned from exile alongside Zerubbabel. He rebuilt the altar of burnt offering before the temple's foundation was even laid, and stood at the head of the priests and Levites through years of opposition until the house was finished.

name: Ezra
roles: the priest and scribe who taught God's law and led Judah's reform
summary: A priest and scribe descended from Aaron who set his heart to study, live, and teach the law of Yahweh. He led a second return from Babylon a generation after Zerubbabel, and when he found the returned exiles intermarried with the surrounding nations against the law, led them in public confession and reform.

name: Nehemiah
roles: the cupbearer who left the palace to rebuild Jerusalem's walls
summary: Cupbearer to king Artaxerxes in Susa, who wept and fasted on hearing that Jerusalem's walls lay broken and its gates burned. Given leave and letters by the king, he inspected the ruins by night, rebuilt the wall in fifty-two days despite mockery and plots against his life, and later returned to enforce reforms the people had let slip.

name: Sanballat
roles: the Samaritan governor who mocked and plotted against the wall-builders
summary: Governor of Samaria and the chief opponent of Jerusalem's rebuilding. He mocked the wall-builders, conspired to attack them, and later tried to lure Nehemiah into a trap and hire a false prophet against him—every attempt failing.

name: Esther
roles: the Jewish orphan who became queen and risked her life for her people
summary: A Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai in the Persian citadel of Susa, chosen queen after Vashti's fall without anyone knowing her people. When Haman's decree threatened every Jew in the empire, she risked her life by approaching the king uninvited, exposed Haman's plot at a banquet, and won a reversal that saved her people — establishing the feast of Purim.

name: Mordecai
roles: the cousin who raised Esther and uncovered Haman's plot
summary: A Jew of the tribe of Benjamin living in Susa who raised his orphaned cousin Esther as his own daughter. He uncovered a plot against the king's life, refused to bow to the newly promoted Haman, and pressed Esther to risk everything for her people — "who knows if you haven't come to the kingdom for such a time as this?" He was honored by the king the very night Haman planned to hang him, and rose to become second only to Ahasuerus.

name: Haman
roles: the official whose plot to destroy the Jews backfired on himself
summary: An official promoted above all the king's other princes, whose fury at Mordecai's one refusal to bow grew into a plot to destroy every Jew in the Persian empire. Exposed by Esther at her own banquet, he was hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai.

name: Ahasuerus
roles: the Persian king whose queen and decrees turned on a hidden secret
summary: The Persian king who deposed Queen Vashti for refusing his summons, chose Esther as her replacement without learning she was a Jew, and — persuaded first by Haman, then reversed by Esther — held the fate of every Jew in his empire in a signet ring.

name: Vashti
roles: the queen deposed for refusing the king's command, opening the way for Esther
summary: Queen of Persia, deposed by King Ahasuerus after she refused to be displayed before his feast — a vacancy that opened the way for Esther to become queen in her place.

name: Job
roles: the blameless man whose faith survived total loss
summary: A blameless and upright man from the land of Uz, the greatest of all the people of the east in wealth and family, tested by catastrophic loss at Satan's challenge and Yahweh's permission. He refused to curse God through the loss of his children, his wealth, and his health, wrestled honestly with God through chapters of grief and his friends' bad theology, and was restored with double what he had before after Yahweh answered him out of the whirlwind.

name: Eliphaz
roles: the friend whose theology Yahweh rebuked by name
summary: The Temanite, first and most prominent of Job's three friends, who insisted Job's suffering must be deserved. Yahweh rebuked him and his companions by name for not speaking rightly about him, and accepted Job's prayer on their behalf only after they offered sacrifices.

name: Jeremiah
roles: the weeping prophet who watched Jerusalem fall exactly as he warned
summary: A priest from Anathoth called as a prophet to the nations while still young -- "before I formed you in the womb, I knew you." He confronted kings and priests with unwelcome warnings for forty years, was thrown into a cistern to die for it, watched Jerusalem fall exactly as he had prophesied, and was carried off to Egypt against his will by the very remnant he had tried to save.

name: Baruch
roles: the scribe who wrote Jeremiah's words and shared his fate
summary: Jeremiah's scribe, who wrote his prophecies onto a scroll from his dictation -- twice, after King Jehoiakim burned the first copy. He stayed with Jeremiah through the fall of Jerusalem and was carried to Egypt alongside him.

name: Ebed-Melech
roles: the Ethiopian official who saved Jeremiah from the cistern
summary: An Ethiopian eunuch in King Zedekiah's court who, alone among the officials, pleaded for Jeremiah's life when he had been left to die in a muddy cistern, then organized his rescue.

name: Gedaliah
roles: the governor appointed over Judah's ruins, assassinated within months
summary: Appointed governor over the remnant left in Judah after Jerusalem's fall. Jeremiah went to live under his protection, but he was assassinated by Ishmael son of Nethaniah within months, throwing the remaining community into panic and flight.

name: Ezekiel
roles: the priest-prophet among the exiles whose visions embodied Israel's coming restoration
summary: A priest carried into exile with Jehoiachin, called by a vision of Yahweh's glory by the river Chebar and made a watchman over Israel -- responsible to warn, though not for whether anyone listens. He acted out the coming siege and exile in his own body, was forbidden to mourn his wife's sudden death as a sign to the people, and saw a valley of dry bones rise up as a living army -- Yahweh's promise that even a nation as dead as scattered bones could live again.

name: Daniel
roles: the exile whose wisdom and faithfulness outlasted four kings
summary: Carried to Babylon as a young noble of Judah, he refused to defile himself with the king's food, was given wisdom to interpret dreams no one else could read, and served faithfully through the reigns of Nebuchadnezzar, Belshazzar, and Darius the Mede -- surviving a night in a lions' den when his only fault was praying toward Jerusalem three times a day.

name: Shadrach
roles: one of three who chose the furnace over bowing to Nebuchadnezzar's image
summary: One of three young Jewish exiles -- with Meshach and Abednego -- who refused to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden image even under threat of a burning fiery furnace, and walked out of the fire unharmed with a fourth figure beside them.

name: Meshach
roles: one of three who chose the furnace over bowing to Nebuchadnezzar's image
summary: One of three young Jewish exiles -- with Shadrach and Abednego -- who refused to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden image even under threat of a burning fiery furnace, and walked out of the fire unharmed with a fourth figure beside them.

name: Abednego
roles: one of three who chose the furnace over bowing to Nebuchadnezzar's image
summary: One of three young Jewish exiles -- with Shadrach and Meshach -- who refused to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden image even under threat of a burning fiery furnace, and walked out of the fire unharmed with a fourth figure beside them.

name: Belshazzar
roles: the king who saw his kingdom's end written on his banquet wall
summary: A later king of Babylon who threw a great feast using the temple's sacred vessels and saw a disembodied hand write his kingdom's end on the wall -- "you are weighed in the balances, and are found wanting." He was killed that same night, and his kingdom fell to the Medes and Persians.

name: Darius the Mede
roles: the king tricked into signing the decree that sent Daniel to the lions
summary: The king who received Belshazzar's fallen kingdom and, flattered into signing a decree forbidding prayer to anyone but himself, was forced by his own unchangeable law to have Daniel thrown to the lions -- then spent a sleepless night hoping for his rescue.

name: Hosea
roles: the prophet whose own marriage became a living picture of God's love for an unfaithful people
summary: A prophet to the northern kingdom of Israel, told to marry a woman who would be unfaithful to him and to keep loving and buying her back even after she left -- his own marriage acting out Yahweh's relentless love for an Israel that kept turning to other gods.

name: Gomer
roles: the wife whose unfaithfulness, and Hosea's love for her anyway, pictured Israel and God
summary: Hosea's wife, whose unfaithfulness to him became a living picture of Israel's unfaithfulness to Yahweh -- and whose being bought back and loved again pictured Yahweh's relentless love for Israel anyway.

name: Amos
roles: the shepherd from Judah sent to confront Israel over injustice
summary: A shepherd and sycamore-fig farmer from Tekoa in Judah, sent by Yahweh to confront the northern kingdom over its injustice to the poor even during a time of prosperity. When the priest Amaziah told him to go prophesy back in his own country, Amos answered that he'd never trained to be a prophet -- Yahweh simply took him from the flock.

name: Jonah
roles: the prophet who fled his own call, then resented the mercy it produced
summary: A prophet sent to warn Nineveh, Israel's enemy, of coming judgment. He fled by ship instead, was thrown overboard in a storm and swallowed by a great fish, then obeyed once given a second chance -- and was furious when Nineveh repented and Yahweh spared the city, since mercy for Israel's enemies was exactly what he'd fled to avoid.

name: Haggai
roles: the prophet whose short, direct messages got the temple's rebuilding moving again
summary: A prophet who confronted the returned exiles for finishing their own houses while Yahweh's temple lay unbuilt, and whose brief, direct messages -- "be strong... and work, for I am with you" -- helped restart the construction Ezra records being finished soon after.

name: Zechariah
roles: the prophet whose visions encouraged the temple's rebuilding alongside Haggai
summary: A prophet who supported Zerubbabel and the returned exiles with a series of visions during the temple's rebuilding, reminding them the work would be finished "not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit."

name: Jesus
roles: the Messiah whose birth, life, death, and resurrection are the center of the New Testament
summary: Conceived by the Holy Spirit and born to Mary in Bethlehem, he grew up in Nazareth, was baptized by his cousin John, and spent roughly three years teaching, healing, and calling people to himself before his death and resurrection in Jerusalem. Called the Messiah, the Son of God, and the Word made flesh.

name: Mary
roles: the virgin who bore Jesus and treasured what she didn't yet understand
summary: A young woman of Nazareth, engaged to Joseph, told by the angel Gabriel she would bear the Messiah by the Holy Spirit. She visited her relative Elizabeth, sang a song of praise anticipating God's reversal of the proud and the lowly, and treasured the things said about her son without fully understanding them.

name: Joseph
roles: the carpenter who protected Mary and Jesus through visions in his sleep
summary: A descendant of David engaged to Mary, who nearly divorced her quietly on finding her pregnant before an angel explained the child was from the Holy Spirit. He named Jesus as instructed, and three more times acted on warnings in his dreams -- fleeing to Egypt, then returning to settle in Nazareth instead of Judea.

name: John the Baptist
roles: the forerunner who prepared the way for Jesus
summary: Son of Zacharias and Elizabeth, born after his father was struck silent for disbelieving the angel's announcement. Grew up to become a wilderness prophet who baptized Jesus and prepared people for his coming, "in the spirit and power of Elijah."

name: Zacharias
roles: the priest struck silent for doubting his son's promised birth
summary: A priest of the division of Abijah who, burning incense in the temple, was told by the angel Gabriel that his elderly, childless wife Elizabeth would bear a son. He doubted and was struck mute until the child was born and named John as instructed, after which he prophesied over his son's future.

name: Elizabeth
roles: Zacharias's wife, whose unlikely pregnancy in old age recognized Mary's greater one
summary: A relative of Mary who conceived John in her old age after decades of barrenness. When the pregnant Mary visited her, the baby leaped in her womb and she was filled with the Holy Spirit, recognizing Mary as "the mother of my Lord" before anyone had told her.

name: Peter
roles: the fisherman who became the foremost of the twelve apostles
summary: A fisherman from Galilee, brought to Jesus by his brother Andrew and renamed Cephas -- Peter, "the rock." After a miraculous catch of fish left him overwhelmed at his own sinfulness, he left everything to follow Jesus and became the most prominent of the twelve.

name: Andrew
roles: the disciple who first brought his brother Peter to Jesus
summary: A fisherman and former disciple of John the Baptist, the first to follow Jesus after hearing John call him "the Lamb of God." He immediately found his brother Simon and brought him to Jesus too.

name: James
roles: one of the sons of Zebedee, part of Jesus's inner circle
summary: A fisherman, son of Zebedee and brother of John, called from his father's boat to follow Jesus after a miraculous catch of fish. Part of Jesus's closest inner circle among the twelve.

name: John
roles: the disciple whose Gospel calls him "the one Jesus loved"
summary: A fisherman, son of Zebedee and brother of James, called from his father's boat to follow Jesus. Part of Jesus's closest inner circle, and traditionally credited with the Gospel of John, three letters, and Revelation.

name: Philip
roles: the disciple who brought Nathanael to Jesus
summary: A disciple from Bethsaida called directly by Jesus, who then found his friend Nathanael and brought him too, answering his skepticism with "come and see."

name: Nathanael
roles: the skeptic Jesus surprised by already knowing him
summary: A man from Cana, skeptical that anything good could come from Nazareth until Jesus told him he had seen him under a fig tree before Philip ever called him -- convincing him instantly that Jesus was the Son of God. Also known as Bartholomew.

name: Nicodemus
roles: the Pharisee who came to Jesus by night and later helped bury him
summary: A Pharisee and ruler of the Jews who came to Jesus secretly at night, unable to understand how someone could be "born again." Jesus used his confusion to explain God's love for the world and the gift of eternal life through the Son. He later helped provide for Jesus's burial.

name: the Samaritan woman
roles: the Samaritan woman whose testimony brought her whole town to Jesus
summary: A woman of Sychar in Samaria, married five times and living with a man who wasn't her husband, whom Jesus met at Jacob's well and offered "living water." Surprised that a Jew would speak to her at all, she recognized him as the Messiah after he described her whole life, then brought her entire town out to meet him.

name: Lazarus
roles: the friend Jesus raised from the dead after four days in the tomb
summary: A man of Bethany, brother of Mary and Martha, whom Jesus loved. He died and had been in the tomb four days by the time Jesus arrived, who then called him back to life in front of a crowd -- the last and greatest of his signs before his own death.

name: Martha
roles: the sister who met Jesus with grief and a confession of faith
summary: Lazarus's sister, who went out to meet Jesus on the road with both grief -- "if you would have been here, my brother wouldn't have died" -- and faith, confessing him as the Christ, the Son of God, before he raised her brother.

name: Mary of Bethany
roles: the sister who fell at Jesus's feet weeping for her brother
summary: Lazarus's sister, who stayed home grieving until Jesus called for her, then fell at his feet with the same words as Martha. Identified in John as the woman who later anointed Jesus's feet with expensive perfume.

name: Thomas
roles: the disciple ready to die with Jesus, later famous for doubting his resurrection
summary: One of the twelve, first mentioned urging the other disciples to go with Jesus into danger at Bethany even if it meant dying with him -- "let's go also, that we may die with him."

name: Zacchaeus
roles: the wealthy tax collector who climbed a tree to see Jesus
summary: A short, wealthy chief tax collector in Jericho, despised for exploiting his own people on Rome's behalf, who climbed a sycamore tree just to see Jesus over the crowd. Jesus invited himself to stay at his house, and Zacchaeus responded by giving half his wealth to the poor and repaying everyone he'd cheated four times over.

name: the rich young ruler
roles: the wealthy man who walked away sad rather than give up his possessions
summary: A young man who kept every commandment from his youth but walked away grieved when Jesus told him to sell everything, give to the poor, and follow him -- unwilling to trade his great wealth for treasure in heaven.

name: Judas Iscariot
roles: the disciple who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver
summary: One of the twelve, treasurer of the group, who agreed to betray Jesus to the chief priests and identified him with a kiss in Gethsemane. His betrayal set in motion Jesus's arrest, trial, and crucifixion.

name: Caiaphas
roles: the high priest who condemned Jesus for blasphemy
summary: The high priest who presided over Jesus's nighttime trial before the Jewish council, tore his own robes at Jesus's claim to be the Son of Man seated at God's right hand, and declared it blasphemy worthy of death.

name: Pilate
roles: the Roman governor who washed his hands of Jesus's death
summary: The Roman governor of Judea who found no real charge against Jesus, tried to release him instead of the convicted Barabbas, and finally caved to the crowd's demand for crucifixion -- washing his hands in a public but empty gesture of innocence.

name: Barabbas
roles: the convicted prisoner released instead of Jesus
summary: A notorious prisoner held by Rome, released by Pilate at the crowd's demand in Jesus's place -- freedom traded directly for Jesus's death.

name: Mary Magdalene
roles: the woman who followed Jesus from Galilee and stayed at the cross
summary: A woman who followed and provided for Jesus from Galilee, present at the cross with the other women when the male disciples had fled -- and, as later curation will cover, the first person to see the risen Jesus.

name: Simon of Cyrene
roles: the man forced to carry Jesus's cross
summary: A man from Cyrene, compelled by Roman soldiers to carry Jesus's cross to Golgotha after Jesus, weakened by the flogging, could no longer carry it himself.

name: the penitent thief
roles: the criminal crucified beside Jesus who was promised paradise
summary: One of two criminals crucified alongside Jesus, who -- unlike the other -- rebuked his fellow criminal's mockery and asked Jesus to remember him in his kingdom. Jesus promised him paradise that very day.

name: Joseph of Arimathea
roles: the secret disciple who gave Jesus his own tomb
summary: A rich man from Arimathea and secret disciple of Jesus who asked Pilate for the body, wrapped it himself, and laid it in his own new, unused tomb cut into the rock.

name: Cleopas
roles: one of two disciples who recognized the risen Jesus in the breaking of bread
summary: One of two disciples walking to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection, joined unknowingly by the risen Jesus, who explained how the Scriptures pointed to his suffering and glory -- recognized only when Jesus broke bread with them at the table.

name: Matthew
roles: the tax collector called from his booth to become one of the twelve
summary: A tax collector -- a profession Jews despised as collaboration with Rome -- called by Jesus with just two words, "follow me." He got up immediately, and his own house feast for "tax collectors and sinners" prompted Jesus's answer to the Pharisees: "I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance." Traditionally credited as the author of the Gospel of Matthew.

name: Matthias
roles: the apostle chosen by lot to replace Judas
summary: A follower of Jesus from the beginning of his ministry, chosen by lot over Joseph called Barsabbas to replace Judas Iscariot as the twelfth apostle.

name: Stephen
roles: the first Christian martyr, who saw Jesus at his death
summary: One of seven men chosen to serve the early church's growing needs, full of the Holy Spirit and known for wonders and unanswerable wisdom. Falsely accused of blasphemy before the council, he saw a vision of Jesus standing at God's right hand just before being stoned to death outside Jerusalem -- dying with words that echoed Jesus's own on the cross: "Lord, don't hold this sin against them."

name: Paul
roles: the persecutor turned apostle who carried the gospel across the Roman world
summary: Originally named Saul, a zealous persecutor of the church who held the coats of those who stoned Stephen and hunted believers from city to city -- until a blinding light and the voice of the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus stopped him entirely. Baptized and filled with the Holy Spirit after three days of blindness, he immediately began proclaiming the very faith he'd tried to destroy, eventually becoming the New Testament's most prolific writer and its most tireless missionary.

name: Cornelius
roles: the Roman centurion whose household became the first Gentile converts
summary: A Roman centurion in Caesarea known for his generosity to the poor and constant prayer, though not a Jew. Told in a vision to send for Peter, his household became the first Gentiles to receive the Holy Spirit and be baptized -- proof, to Peter and the watching Jewish believers, that God's promise wasn't for Israel alone.

name: Barnabas
roles: the encourager who first vouched for Paul and partnered with him in ministry
summary: A Levite from Cyprus whose name means "son of encouragement," one of the first to accept the converted Saul when the other disciples were still afraid of him. Set apart with Paul by the Holy Spirit for missionary work, he became his partner on the first missionary journey and a key voice at the Jerusalem council.

name: Silas
roles: Paul's companion who sang hymns with him in a Philippian jail
summary: A leading member of the Jerusalem church who accompanied Paul on his second missionary journey after his split with Barnabas. Imprisoned alongside Paul in Philippi, he was singing hymns with him at midnight when an earthquake shook open the prison doors.

name: the Philippian jailer
roles: the jailer who nearly killed himself before asking how to be saved
summary: A Roman jailer in Philippi who, waking to find the prison doors open after an earthquake, drew his sword to kill himself rather than face the consequences of an escape -- until Paul called out that all the prisoners were still there. He asked what he must do to be saved, and he and his whole household were baptized that same night.

name: Abner
summary: Commander of Saul's army; keeps Saul's son Ishbosheth on the throne for two years after Saul's death, then breaks with him and offers to bring all Israel over to David -- but is murdered by Joab before it can happen, in revenge for killing Joab's brother Asahel.

name: Asahel
summary: The third son of Zeruiah, "as light of foot as a wild gazelle." Pursues Abner in battle and is killed by him -- his death starts the blood feud that ends with Joab murdering Abner.

name: Abishai
summary: One of the three sons of Zeruiah and a recurring army commander alongside his brother Joab -- present when Asahel is killed, wants to kill Shimei for cursing David, and helps put down Sheba's rebellion.

name: Ahithophel
summary: David's trusted counselor -- his advice was regarded "as if a man inquired at the inner sanctuary of God" -- who joins Absalom's rebellion. His sound military advice is passed over for Hushai's, and seeing his counsel rejected, he goes home and hangs himself.

name: Hushai
summary: David's friend, sent back into Jerusalem at David's own request to pose as Absalom's supporter and undermine Ahithophel's counsel from the inside -- and does, buying David the time he needs.

name: Ittai
summary: A Philistine commander from Gath, a recent exile in David's service. When David urges him to stay behind rather than share his exile during Absalom's revolt, he refuses: "in what place my lord the king is, whether for death or for life, your servant will be there also."

name: Shimei
summary: A relative of Saul's who curses David and pelts him with stones as he flees Jerusalem during Absalom's revolt, calling him a man of blood. David restrains Abishai from killing him on the spot; when David returns victorious, Shimei begs for mercy and is spared.

name: Amasa
roles: commander, first for Absalom then for David
summary: Commanded Absalom's rebel army; afterward David appoints him over his own army in place of Joab, as a gesture of reconciliation. Sent to muster troops against Sheba's rebellion, he is treacherously killed by Joab, who never accepted being replaced.

name: Sheba
roles: led a rebellion after Absalom's death
summary: A Benjamite who blows the trumpet and calls Israel away from David ("we have no portion in David") in a fresh revolt right on the heels of Absalom's. Pursued to Abel Beth Maacah, where the city's wise woman ends the siege by having him beheaded.

name: The wise woman of Abel
summary: Unnamed but real, like the widow of Zarephath -- when Joab besieges Abel Beth Maacah hunting Sheba, she negotiates with him from the wall, persuades the city to hand over Sheba's head instead of being destroyed, and the siege ends without further bloodshed.

name: Priscilla
summary: A Jewish Christian, exiled from Rome with her husband Aquila under Claudius's decree. The couple host Paul, travel with him, and take the eloquent-but-incomplete teacher Apollos aside to "explain to him the way of God more accurately." Paul later writes that they "risked their own necks" for his life.

name: Aquila
summary: Priscilla's husband, a Jew of Pontus. Always named together with his wife in Acts and the epistles -- they share one trade, one household, and one ministry of hosting and teaching.

name: Apollos
summary: An eloquent Alexandrian, "mighty in the Scriptures," who taught accurately about Jesus but knew only the baptism of John until Priscilla and Aquila corrected him. His later ministry in Corinth was effective enough that a faction there claimed him over Paul -- "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase," Paul answers.

name: Lydia
summary: A dealer in purple cloth from Thyatira, already a worshiper of God when Paul reaches Philippi. "The Lord opened her heart to listen" -- she and her household are baptized, and she persuades Paul's company to stay in her home, becoming the first convert and host of the church in Europe.

name: John Mark
summary: Joins Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary journey, then withdraws partway through and returns to Jerusalem. When Barnabas wants to give him another chance, Paul refuses -- "the contention grew so sharp that they separated from each other." Years later, in his last letter, Paul asks for Mark by name: "he is useful to me for service."

name: Timothy
roles: Paul's true child in the faith
summary: A young disciple from Lystra, son of a believing Jewish mother and a Greek father, whom Paul takes on as a close companion and sends on some of his most sensitive missions. Two epistles are addressed to him directly -- "let no man despise your youth."

name: Titus
summary: A trusted delegate Paul sends into difficult situations -- his arrival in Macedonia after a hard stretch in Corinth brings Paul real comfort ("God, who comforts the lowly, comforted us by the coming of Titus"), and he's later left in Crete to put the young church there in order. An epistle is addressed to him.

name: Onesimus
roles: a runaway slave, become a brother
summary: A slave who ran from his master Philemon and, in Rome, becomes Paul's own "child... in my chains." Paul sends him back with a letter -- not commanding Philemon to free him, but appealing to receive him "no longer as a slave, but... a beloved brother," and offering to personally cover whatever he owes.

name: Philemon
summary: A believer, host of a church in his own house, and Onesimus's owner -- the recipient of Paul's shortest and most personal letter, an appeal on Onesimus's behalf rather than an order, written with confidence he "will do even beyond what I say."

name: Demas
summary: Once counted among Paul's fellow workers; in Paul's last letter, named as having left him, "having loved this present world" -- a small, unadorned note of the cost of staying faithful to the end.

name: Reuben
summary: Jacob's firstborn son by Leah. Tries quietly to save Joseph from his brothers by suggesting the pit instead of murder, and later offers his own two sons as collateral to bring Benjamin back safely -- but sleeping with his father's concubine Bilhah costs him his birthright preeminence, which Jacob names outright on his deathbed.

name: Simeon
summary: Jacob's second son by Leah. With his brother Levi, kills every man of Shechem in revenge for their sister Dinah's assault. Years later, Joseph holds him hostage in Egypt to force the brothers to bring Benjamin.

name: Levi
summary: Jacob's third son by Leah. With his brother Simeon, kills every man of Shechem in revenge for their sister Dinah's assault -- violence Jacob condemns even on his deathbed, though Levi's own descendants (Moses, Aaron) later become the priestly line.

name: Judah
roles: the messianic line runs through him
summary: Jacob's fourth son by Leah. Proposes selling Joseph rather than killing him; later fathers Perez by his own daughter-in-law Tamar without recognizing her, and admits "she is more righteous than I." Becomes the brother who pledges his own life as collateral for Benjamin and delivers the speech that finally breaks Joseph's composure. Jacob's blessing names him the one the scepter belongs to.

name: Benjamin
summary: Rachel's second son, born as she died, and Joseph's only full brother. His presence in Egypt is what Joseph tests his brothers over, and his safe return is what Judah stakes his own life on.

name: Bilhah
summary: Rachel's servant, given to Jacob to bear children on Rachel's behalf -- mother of Dan and Naphtali. Reuben's affair with her after Rachel's death is a serious violation that costs him his birthright standing.

name: Zilpah
summary: Leah's servant, given to Jacob the same way Bilhah was given by Rachel -- mother of Gad and Asher.

name: Dinah
summary: Jacob's only named daughter. Assaulted by Shechem while visiting the women of the land; her brothers Simeon and Levi avenge her by killing every man of his city.

name: Shechem
summary: Son of Hamor, ruler of the Hivite city that bears his family's name. Assaults Dinah, then wants to marry her; agrees along with every man of his city to be circumcised to make the marriage possible, and is killed by Simeon and Levi while still recovering.

name: Tamar
summary: Married to Judah's firstborn Er, then to his brother Onan under the custom of raising up an heir; when Judah withholds his third son from her, she disguises herself and conceives by Judah himself. Confronted, Judah says "she is more righteous than I" -- her son Perez becomes an ancestor of David.

name: Laban
summary: Rebekah's brother, and Rachel and Leah's father. Substitutes Leah for Rachel on the wedding night after Jacob's seven years of work, then extracts seven more -- the same trick of substitution Jacob himself once played on his own father.

name: Potiphar
summary: An Egyptian official who buys Joseph and puts him in charge of his whole household -- then, believing his wife's accusation, has him thrown in prison.

name: Potiphar's wife
summary: Unnamed in the text. Repeatedly propositions Joseph, who refuses on the grounds that it would be "sin against God"; when he flees leaving his garment behind, she uses it to falsely accuse him, and he's imprisoned.

name: Abraham's servant
summary: Unnamed in the text (Genesis 24), the senior servant Abraham sends to find a wife for Isaac among his own relatives rather than the Canaanites. Prays for a specific sign, meets Rebekah at the well exactly as he'd asked, and gives Yahweh credit at every step: "Yahweh has led me on the way."

name: Pharaoh's cupbearer
summary: Imprisoned alongside Joseph; Joseph correctly interprets his dream as restoration to Pharaoh's service within three days. Restored exactly as foretold -- but forgets Joseph completely until Pharaoh's own dreams force the memory back two years later.

name: Pharaoh's baker
summary: Imprisoned alongside Joseph and the cupbearer; Joseph correctly interprets his dream too, but as execution rather than restoration -- the same three days, opposite outcomes.

name: Nabal
summary: A rich sheep-owner, "surly and evil in his doings," who refuses David's request for provisions after David's men had protected his flocks -- an insult that nearly gets his whole household killed until his wife Abigail intervenes.

name: Abigail
summary: "Intelligent and had a beautiful face" -- when her husband Nabal insults David, she rides out herself with provisions and talks David out of bloodshed before he even knows what she's done. Ten days later Nabal dies, and David marries her.

name: Doeg
summary: An Edomite in Saul's service who witnesses Ahimelech helping David, then reports it -- and, when Saul's own guards refuse to raise a hand against the priests, personally kills eighty-five of them and puts the entire priestly city of Nob to the sword.

name: Ahimelech
summary: Gives the fleeing David consecrated bread and Goliath's own sword, not knowing he's defying Saul by doing it. Defends himself plainly to Saul's face -- "who among all your servants is so faithful as David?" -- and is killed for it along with the rest of Nob's priests.

name: Abiathar
summary: The one son of Ahimelech to escape Doeg's massacre, fleeing to David with the news. David takes responsibility for his father's death and keeps him close -- Abiathar becomes his priest for the rest of David's reign.

name: Achish
summary: The Philistine king David first fools by feigning madness, then later serves as a vassal for over a year while hiding from Saul. Genuinely trusts David -- "you have been upright... as an angel of God" -- and is the one who has to send him home before the battle at Gilboa, at his own commanders' insistence.

name: Jethro
summary: Visits Moses in the wilderness and watches him single-handedly judge every dispute in Israel from morning to evening. Tells him plainly, "the thing that you do is not good... you will surely wear away" -- and proposes the tiered system of judges over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens that Moses actually adopts.

name: Shiphrah
summary: One of the two named midwives Pharaoh orders to kill every Hebrew baby boy at birth. Defies him because she "feared God" -- her act of civil disobedience is what keeps the Hebrew population, and eventually Moses himself, alive.

name: Puah
summary: The second of the two named midwives who defy Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew baby boys. Named individually alongside Shiphrah -- God "dealt well with the midwives... and gave them families."

name: Phinehas
summary: Stops a plague that's already killing thousands of Israelites during the Baal Peor apostasy by personally executing an Israelite man and a Midianite woman in the act. Yahweh explicitly rewards his zeal with "my covenant of peace" and an everlasting priesthood for his line.

name: Mahlah
summary: One of Zelophehad's five daughters, who together petition Moses for the right to inherit their father's land since he died with no sons -- a request Yahweh rules is right, changing Israel's inheritance law.

name: Noah
summary: One of Zelophehad's five daughters, individually named alongside her sisters in both the original petition and the later ruling on tribal land -- her name distinct from, and long before, the flood's Noah.

name: Hoglah
summary: One of Zelophehad's five daughters who petition Moses for their father's inheritance.

name: Milcah
summary: One of Zelophehad's five daughters who petition Moses for their father's inheritance -- her name distinct from the earlier Milcah, Abraham's brother Nahor's wife.

name: Tirzah
summary: One of Zelophehad's five daughters who petition Moses for their father's inheritance.
